title: Fruit Only Diet
hook: What if you ate only fruit?
banner:
WHAT IF YOU ATE
ONLY FRUIT?
scene: kitchen table with a bowl of mixed fruit

beats.label: DAY 1
beats.line: After day one, blood sugar spikes, then you feel a crash.
beats.idea: Close‑up of a glowing glucose gauge jumping as the character's hand trembles.

beats.label: DAY 3
beats.line: By day three, a sticky film forms on your teeth from sugar.
beats.idea: A sugary film coats the character's teeth in a mirror.

beats.label: DAY 7
beats.line: At day seven, excess fiber causes uncomfortable gas and bloating.
beats.idea: Belly inflates slightly, showing a swirl of fiber.

beats.label: DAY 14
beats.line: By day fourteen, insufficient protein triggers muscle fatigue and soreness.
beats.idea: Muscles appear frail with a shrinking strength bar.

beats.label: DAY 30
beats.line: After a month, constant fructose builds fat in your liver.
beats.idea: Liver illustration fills with yellow fat spots.

description: A quick visual look at the physiological changes from an all‑fruit diet.

facts.claim: Consuming a high‑sugar diet can cause rapid increases in blood glucose levels.
Frequent exposure to sugars promotes dental plaque formation and can lead to cavities.
High dietary fiber intake may cause gastrointestinal bloating and gas.
Inadequate protein intake can result in muscle mass loss over time.
facts.source: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

facts.claim: Consistently high fructose consumption is linked to non‑alcoholic fatty liver disease.

end.line: Could you survive on fruit alone?

topic: What happens if you eat only fruit?
